spatial_claims.claim: Two concentric circles with center E; greater circle ABCD contains lesser circle FGHK; EF is radius of lesser circle
BD is a diameter through E; AC is perpendicular to BD through E and also a diameter; A,B,C,D divide the circle into four equal quarter-arcs
EF < EB since the lesser circle lies inside the greater
EL bisects angle AEB, meeting the greater circle at L; EM bisects angle LEB, meeting circle at M; repeated bisection produces smaller arcs
Perpendicular from E to chord increases as subtended arc decreases (from r^2 = d^2 + (c/2)^2)
Perpendicular EQ from E to chord BN satisfies EQ > EF after sufficient bisections
Arc BN is (1/2^n)-th of a quarter-circle; full circle divided into 4*2^n equal arcs
Equal arcs marked around entire circle; consecutive division points joined to form inscribed polygon
By symmetry of regular polygon centered at E, perpendicular from E to every side equals EQ > EF
Each side lies entirely outside the lesser circle because perpendicular distance from E to each side exceeds EF

configuration_map: Center E is shared by both circles. The greater circle has radius EB, the lesser has radius EF, with EF < EB. Points A, B, C, D lie on the greater circle at the endpoints of two perpendicular diameters AC and BD. Successive bisection of arc AB (a quarter-arc, subtending 90 degrees at E) produces points L, M, ..., N on the greater circle, with arc BN = 90/2^n degrees. Point Q is the foot of the perpendicular from E to chord BN, lying on chord BN between B and N. The perpendicular distance EQ = EB*cos(arc_BN/2) increases toward EB as the arc decreases. After sufficient bisection, EQ > EF. The polygon formed by marking off 4*2^n equal arcs around the full circle is regular and centered at E, with each side at perpendicular distance EQ from E, placing all sides outside the lesser circle.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The key geometric relationships (perpendicular from center to chord increases as arc decreases; this perpendicular can be made to exceed EF; regular polygon symmetry ensures uniform perpendicular distance; perpendicular exceeding inner radius implies no intersection) are all compatible. No point is placed in contradictory positions across steps, and no angle decomposition or betweenness claim conflicts with the established configuration.
